emergence.summary: A single-gene HTT CAG-repeat EXPANSION in exon 1 produces a polyglutamine huntingtin with a dominant TOXIC gain-of-function that progressively impairs striatal (medium spiny) neuron homeostasis and survival -- a pathological BRAKE on the neuronal program -- so the striatal-neuron axis is driven DOWN. The lesion is a CODING repeat expansion, not a promoter change (exactly like sickle cell's coding missense): the promoter gamma read here is of the HTT LOCUS switch structure, and the disease direction is forced by the toxic gain-of-function biology. Longer repeats -> earlier onset (the repeat-length/dosage axis), but the repeat tract itself is not read from the promoter window. An approved SYMPTOMATIC therapy for chorea exists (VMAT2 inhibitors) but does not address the HTT switch; no disease-modifying therapy is yet approved. Magnitude [O].

grades.perturbation_direction: [F] forced by (role x mechanism); cited biology
grades.perturbation_magnitude: [O] OPEN -- how far the switch moves is runtime/Layer-2, not sequence-derivable

per_gene.note: An expanded CAG tract (commonly >36 repeats) in HTT exon 1 yields polyglutamine-huntingtin that acts as a dominant TOXIC gain-of-function -- a pathological brake on striatal neuronal homeostasis (proteostasis / mitochondrial / transcriptional dysregulation and aggregation) -> neuronal function and survival suppressed. The promoter gamma reads the locus switch STRUCTURE only; it does NOT encode the CAG-repeat coding lesion (firewall), exactly as for HBB's coding missense. Repeat length sets onset but is not read from the promoter window.

falsifiers.claim: mutant HTT (CAG expansion, toxic GOF) lowers the striatal-neuron homeostasis/survival axis
falsifiers.falsifier: a CAG-expanded HTT allele that PRESERVED or IMPROVED striatal neuron survival/function would refute the toxic-brake direction
falsifiers.measurable_by: striatal medium-spiny-neuron survival / striatal volume by CAG-length genotype in an HTT-expansion model

falsifiers.claim: lowering mutant huntingtin (reduce HTT) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if HTT-lowering WORSENED or failed to improve striatal neuronal survival/function, the reduce-HTT lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: striatal neuron survival / motor-behaviour response to HTT-lowering in an HTT-expansion model
